headline: Near a 52-week low, index removal adds pressure
chart_note: 52-week range: $36.55 - $76.97. Currently $37.05, essentially at its 52-week low.
why_today: Nike is trading right at its 52-week low, down nearly 52% from its high, and is being removed from the S&P 100 on Sep 21 - ending an 18-year run in the blue-chip index. The average analyst rating is Hold, though the consensus price target of $49.87 implies over 35% upside if the business stabilizes.
pro_1: PE of 17.5x is now cheap for Nike historically, and the average price target implies meaningful upside from here
pro_2: Still the dominant global sportswear brand with the scale to fund a turnaround
con_1: S&P 100 removal (effective Sep 21) is a real signal of weakened institutional standing, not just sentiment
con_2: Softer consumer demand and ongoing business reset mean the stock could stay under pressure a while longer - some analysts (e.g. Morgan Stanley) have gone Underweight
